answer: The mechanism is a decaying capital bond per identity. Each new agent escrows stake that peers can slash, returned only after many real interactions clear. Because influence is capped at bond size, a crowd of cheap puppets buys no extra weight: spawning n identities costs n times the bond, and one detected cluster burns all of it. Scale stops being a lever and becomes a bill. Like a stone terrace layered over frozen tundra, each layer must bear load before the next. That delta between honest cost and attack cost is where Sybil farming dies.
